_about: The short-form formats and their cards. Every post's format card belongs to one of these. Cards whose beats aren't written yet fill in as Studio breaks posts down (those go in cards.json). Edit this file to add your own.

formats.name: Problem Solution
formats.idea_has: A pain people know, and a fix I use

cards.name: Problem Solution
cards.use_when: there's a pain people know, and a fix I actually use.
cards.needs: a fix I've really used, in steps. No real fix → don't use this format.

beats.name: Hook
beats.job: the pain and a promise of a fix, in one line.

beats.name: Name the fix
beats.job: a short name, so people have something to wait for.

beats.name: Why the usual way fails
beats.job: 1 or 2 lines. The reframe lands here.

beats.name: Steps
beats.job: 2 to 4 plain steps, clearly ordered. Each one a small payoff.

beats.name: Why it works
beats.job: the simple reason. This is the "oh" moment.

beats.name: Proof
beats.job: a result, or who else it worked for. [missing] if none.

beats.name: CTA
beats.job: optional. One ask that helps them do the steps.

flex: Beats 5 and 6 can merge.
Beat 3 can be one line.
If you can show the result on screen, show it right after the hook and drop beat 6.

formats.name: Tutorial
formats.idea_has: A result I can teach people to make, in steps

cards.name: Quick steps
cards.use_when: 3 to 5 short steps get someone to a clear result.
cards.needs: a process I actually use, ideally shown on screen. No real process → don't use this format.
cards.reframe: beat 2, right after the promise. Never line 1.

beats.name: Result promise
beats.job: what they'll make, and how fast or easy, in one line.

beats.name: The surprising part
beats.job: optional. What's odd or annoying about the usual way.

beats.name: "Here's how"
beats.job: one short line that signals the steps.

beats.name: Steps
beats.job: 3 to 5 steps, one line each, shown on screen. A small payoff every step.

beats.name: Output
beats.job: show what they end up with. The payoff, saved for last.

beats.name: Ease line and CTA
beats.job: "that's it", then one ask that helps them do it.

flex: Beat 2 can drop for a plain how-to.
Beat 3 can sit at the end of beat 1.
Beats 5 and 6 can merge ("And there's your content plan.").

cards.name: Live build
cards.use_when: I'm building or running something on screen, and seeing it work is the payoff.
cards.needs: a real build I can screen record start to finish. No footage → use Card A.
cards.length: 2 to 3 minutes, as long as the build takes.
cards.reframe: only after the final reveal, if at all. Never line 1.

beats.name: Big promise
beats.job: what you can build, and how fast. Sets up "can it really?"

beats.name: Start live
beats.job: the first action on screen, right away.

beats.name: Progress
beats.job: wait, then show what came out, with a real reaction.

beats.name: Go bigger
beats.job: the next step, bigger than the last.

beats.name: Final reveal
beats.job: the finished thing working, on screen. The payoff.

beats.name: Ease line
beats.job: one line that says it was easy, or what's next.

flex: Beat 1 can be a stunt ("just wiped this entire MacBook Pro").
Repeat beats 3 and 4 as many times as the build needs.
An honest flaw is fine. It keeps it real.
Beat 6 can tease the next part instead.

formats.name: Common Trap / Mistake
formats.idea_has: A habit or piece of advice that quietly costs people

cards.name: Common Trap / Mistake
cards.use_when: popular advice or a habit sounds right but quietly costs people.
cards.needs: a fix I actually use. An "I used to" moment helps but isn't required. No real fix → don't use this format.
cards.length: 20 to 60 seconds, about 5 to 12 lines. Can be as short as 3 lines.
cards.reframe: beat 1. The trap, named bluntly, is the reframe.

beats.name: Warning hook
beats.job: the trap, named bluntly in line 1, said to "you", so people check if they do it.

beats.name: Open loop
beats.job: admit it sounds odd or backwards, and say the fix is coming.

beats.name: The cost
beats.job: what the trap does to you, in plain "you" terms. An "I used to" moment fits here.

beats.name: The fix, named
beats.job: what to do instead, with a short 2 to 3 word name.

beats.name: Proof
beats.job: a named person, a number or a result. [missing] if none.

beats.name: How
beats.job: 1 to 3 plain steps, usable today.

beats.name: Takeaway and CTA
beats.job: one line someone could repeat to a friend. Then the ask, optional.

flex: Beats 1 and 4 can sit back to back ("You don't need X. You just need Y.").
If the hook already has a number, beat 5 can drop.
Quick version: only beats 1, 3 and 4.

formats.name: Breakdowns / Explainers
formats.idea_has: Why something really happens, how a way of thinking works, or a shift with named examples

cards.name: How it works
cards.use_when: one thing works in a way most people don't expect, and I can explain the cause.
cards.needs: a real example, or a comparison of my own. Missing → don't use this format.
cards.reframe: beat 3, as "what people assume vs what's really going on".

beats.name: Hook
beats.job: a surprising fact, number or thing on screen. Never a vague opinion.

beats.name: Open loop
beats.job: one line that says the answer is coming ("all because of this tiny detail").

beats.name: Name it
beats.job: what people assume, then a short name for what's really going on.

beats.name: How it works
beats.job: the cause in plain steps. Each line answers the one before.

beats.name: Proof
beats.job: a real example or number, so it's believable.

beats.name: Limit and so what
beats.job: where it stops, then what to do. One line each.

beats.name: CTA
beats.job: optional. One soft ask, or a question to the comments.

flex: Beats 1 and 2 can be one line.
If the hook already proves it, drop beat 5.
Beat 7 can drop.

cards.name: Trend or prediction
cards.use_when: I'm calling a shift that's happening now, and I have named examples to back it.
cards.needs: 2 or 3 real names or numbers. "There's data" with none shown doesn't count.
cards.reframe: beat 1. A prediction is already an arguable claim.

beats.name: Hook
beats.job: the shift or prediction as a bold claim.

beats.name: The flip
beats.job: what replaces it, then "here's why".

beats.name: Old rule
beats.job: what used to be true, so the change feels real.

beats.name: Why it's changing
beats.job: the cause in plain words.

beats.name: Proof
beats.job: 2 or 3 named examples or numbers, each one making it more real.

beats.name: The bigger part
beats.job: the more surprising point, saved for late.

beats.name: So what
beats.job: what to do, said softly. CTA optional.

flex: Beat 6 can drop.
Beat 7 can be one line with no ask ("I'm not saying you need to do it. I'm saying it's something you should consider.").

formats.name: Listicle
formats.idea_has: A few tips or options that sit side by side

cards.name: Listicle
cards.use_when: I have 3 to 5 tips or options that sit side by side.
cards.needs: a real reason or example for each item. Missing → cut the item, or don't use this format.
cards.reframe: beat 5, the wrap. Or beat 4, if the last item is the unpopular one. The number is the opener, not the reframe.

beats.name: Promise
beats.job: the number, what it is, and a twist, in line 1 ("5 boring habits that will change your life").

beats.name: Item 1
beats.job: a strong one. Short name, then one line of why or a demo.

beats.name: Middle items
beats.job: short name and one line each. Keeps the count moving.

beats.name: Last item
beats.job: the best or most surprising one, signaled as last ("And last but not least").

beats.name: Wrap
beats.job: one line that ties them together, so there's one thing to remember.

beats.name: CTA
beats.job: optional. One ask.

flex: Strongest item first or last, never in the middle.
The CTA can go just before the last item, so people still stay for it.
An item can be a template plus a filled example, or a demo.
Beat 5 can drop. End on the last item.

formats.name: A vs B
formats.idea_has: Two or three things to compare

cards.name: Side by side
cards.use_when: my point is a contrast between two ways of doing something, or two kinds of people, and they can be compared on the same few things.
cards.needs: one real example, number or story that shows the difference, mine or someone else's. Missing → don't use this format.
cards.reframe: beat 5, the verdict. Never line 1, or the winner is given away.

beats.name: Name A and B
beats.job: name both, or ask which one wins. Stay neutral, so they pick a side.

beats.name: Why it matters
beats.job: one line on why the difference is worth knowing.

beats.name: Contrasts
beats.job: 3 to 5 lines, each on the same thing. "A does X. B does Y." Same rhythm every time.

beats.name: The catch
beats.job: the part most people miss, backed by a real example, number or story.

beats.name: Verdict
beats.job: which one wins, or why both lose.

beats.name: CTA
beats.job: optional. One short ask.

flex: Three options work too ("Reels get followers, carousels get engagement. Stories get leads.").
A bad, good, perfect ladder works too.
Beats 2 and 4 can drop under 30 seconds, but then it reads like a list.
No "how to be the winner" steps. End on the verdict.

cards.name: Story build
cards.use_when: each option has a history or a problem behind it, and each one goes a step further than the last.
cards.needs: a real fact, date or number for each option. Missing → use Card A.

beats.name: Setup
beats.job: say how many things, and that each solves a different problem.

beats.name: First one
beats.job: its problem and its fix, with a specific date or number. Earns trust early.

beats.name: Next one
beats.job: same pattern, plus what it really is under the surface.

beats.name: Last one
beats.job: the most surprising one, pushed furthest. Give it a name.

beats.name: Verdict
beats.job: it's not about which is best, it's about what you value. One short line.

flex: Two items work if the second clearly goes further.
No CTA needed. The verdict is the ending.

formats.name: Scenarios
formats.idea_has: A "what if", or a bold claim people will doubt plus a plan

cards.name: What-if walkthrough
cards.use_when: a "what if" makes the point vivid, and the answer breaks the obvious guess.
cards.needs: a real twist. No twist → it's an explainer, use Breakdowns instead.
cards.reframe: beat 1, only if the reframe is a real what-if people want answered. Otherwise beat 6.

beats.name: The what-if
beats.job: the question, in one line.

beats.name: The guesses
beats.job: 2 or 3 things people would guess, or "it's impossible".

beats.name: Walk through it
beats.job: what happens, step by step. Each step makes them ask "then what?"

beats.name: The twist
beats.job: the thing that breaks the obvious guess.

beats.name: The answer
beats.job: the payoff, saved for last.

beats.name: Tie-back
beats.job: optional. One line linking it to real life, or a soft CTA.

flex: Beat 2 can be the common belief instead of guesses ("it's literally impossible").
Beat 6 can drop. End on the answer.
Specific numbers make it real ("about 21 minutes", "3.6 million").
No lesson after the answer.

cards.name: Bold claim or idea
cards.use_when: my point is a claim or an idea people will doubt, and I have a plan to back it.
cards.needs: a real plan with specifics. Missing → don't use this card.
cards.reframe: beat 3, where you answer the doubt.

beats.name: Bold claim
beats.job: the claim in one line, with a number or timeframe if you have one.

beats.name: Hear me out
beats.job: a short pattern or setup that makes it sound less crazy.

beats.name: The doubt
beats.job: say their doubt out loud, then answer it with 2 or 3 reasons.

beats.name: How I'd do it
beats.job: the plan in clear steps, with specifics. The payoff.

beats.name: Last line
beats.job: a short punchy line, or one ask that hands them the plan.

flex: Beat 2 can drop. Go straight to the plan.
If the claim needs trust, beat 2 can be your background. Keep it humble.
Beat 5 can be a CTA if it gives them the full method.

formats.name: Q&A
formats.idea_has: A real question someone asked me

cards.name: Answer first
cards.use_when: there's a question people actually ask, and my answer is short, blunt and not the popular one.
cards.needs: a real question someone asked me, in comments, DMs or a conversation. Missing → use Breakdowns instead.
cards.reframe: beat 5, the last line. Not a summary.

beats.name: The question
beats.job: the real question, in their words, with specifics.

beats.name: Short answer
beats.job: one blunt line.

beats.name: The reason
beats.job: why, in plain words, plus a real example if you have one.

beats.name: The "but if"
beats.job: who the answer changes for. Makes it feel fair.

beats.name: Sharp last line
beats.job: the answer again as one short line they could quote.

beats.name: CTA
beats.job: optional. Most samples have none.

flex: Beat 4 can drop.
Beat 3 can turn the answer on the viewer ("it's not your talent, it's your presence").

cards.name: Work it out
cards.use_when: the answer needs numbers or steps, and it's more fun to watch me get there.
cards.needs: a real question, plus the real numbers or steps to work it out. Missing → use Card A.

beats.name: The question
beats.job: the real question, with the numbers in it.

beats.name: Let's work it out
beats.job: one line that says you'll work it out now.

beats.name: The working
beats.job: step by step, with real numbers. Each line builds toward the answer.

beats.name: The answer
beats.job: the first answer, said plainly.

beats.name: The follow-up
beats.job: the next question people ask, and the new answer.

flex: The working can be a source you read from, with a promise up front.
End on the thing you promised, or a personal reveal.
No CTA needed.

formats.name: Hero's Journey
formats.idea_has: A time I went from stuck to better

cards.name: Classic climb
cards.use_when: I was stuck, I tried the usual way, then one change got me a result I can put a number on.
cards.needs: a real story with a clear low point. Missing → don't use this format.
cards.length: 30 seconds to 1:30, about 8 to 20 lines. Up to 2:30 only when the personal stakes are very strong.
cards.reframe: beat 6, after the result. Never line 1, or you give away the ending.

beats.name: Low point
beats.job: where I was stuck, with a time, a number or a person who doubted me.

beats.name: Stakes
beats.job: why it mattered to me.

beats.name: What I tried that didn't work
beats.job: one line on the effort that failed.

beats.name: The turn
beats.job: "Until..." the one specific thing I changed.

beats.name: Result
beats.job: what changed, with a number.

beats.name: Reframe
beats.job: one line on where most people go wrong.

beats.name: CTA
beats.job: optional. One ask tied to the turn.

flex: Beat 3 can be one line.
Beat 2 can merge into beat 1 if line 1 already says why it matters.
Drop beat 7 if there's nothing useful to give.
For a long story, bring back an object from the start near the end.

cards.name: Result first
cards.use_when: the finished thing is the hook, and the effort behind it was hidden or hard.
cards.needs: a real result people can see, and the real effort behind it. Missing → don't use this card.
cards.reframe: beat 7, after the full payoff, only if there's a real one.

beats.name: Result first
beats.job: say or show the finished thing in line 1.

beats.name: Quick tease
beats.job: a short glimpse of the reaction, then cut away.

beats.name: The hidden effort
beats.job: how long and how hard, with a time.

beats.name: The obstacle
beats.job: what blocked the easy way.

beats.name: What I did instead
beats.job: the workaround or method, plain.

beats.name: Full payoff
beats.job: the full reveal, held to the end. Pays off the tease.

beats.name: Reframe
beats.job: optional. One line after the payoff.

flex: Beats 4 and 5 can merge.
A side story only fits if it's short and makes them more curious.
No CTA, or one soft line.

formats.name: Personal Learning
formats.idea_has: Something that surprised me

cards.name: Expected vs surprise
cards.use_when: something I did taught me something people wouldn't expect. I went in thinking one thing, and something else turned out to be true.
cards.needs: a real experience. Missing → don't use this format.
cards.reframe: beat 6, right before the CTA. Never line 1, or you give away the surprise.

beats.name: The situation
beats.job: what I was doing, with a number or time, and a hint it didn't go as planned.

beats.name: What I expected
beats.job: what I thought would happen, or what everyone says.

beats.name: The surprise
beats.job: "But..." the thing I didn't see coming.

beats.name: What it was like
beats.job: one concrete detail or result. Shown, not just stated.

beats.name: What it changed
beats.job: what I see or do differently now. About me, not advice to you.

beats.name: Reframe
beats.job: one line on where most people have it wrong.

beats.name: CTA
beats.job: optional. One soft ask or a series sign-off.

flex: Beats 4 and 5 can merge.
Beat 6 can drop if beat 5 already lands it.
Drop beat 7 if it feels tacked on.
For a test or experiment, show the plain version first and the surprising one last.

cards.name: Lessons from a goal
cards.use_when: I set a goal, hit it (or almost), and it taught me things I didn't expect.
cards.needs: a real goal, with start and current numbers. Missing → use Card A.

beats.name: The goal
beats.job: what I set out to do, and when.

beats.name: Before and now
beats.job: where I started and where I am, with numbers.

beats.name: The promise
beats.job: how many lessons, and that they're not what you'd guess.

beats.name: Lesson 1
beats.job: the first surprise, with a real detail from my day.

beats.name: Lesson 2
beats.job: the bigger surprise, with numbers. What I pictured vs what it's really like.

beats.name: Reframe
beats.job: one line on what the goal really gave me.

beats.name: Sign-off
beats.job: optional. A series sign-off or one soft ask.

flex: Two lessons is the most. Save the bigger one for last.
Beat 7 can drop.

formats.name: Case Studies
formats.idea_has: One real result, mine, a user's or someone else's

cards.name: Case Studies
cards.use_when: I can break down one real result, mine, a user's or someone else's.
cards.needs: a real, sourced example with a number.

formats.name: Ranking / Tier List
formats.idea_has: Several options I want to judge

cards.name: Ranking / Tier List
cards.use_when: I'm comparing several options fast.
cards.needs: honest opinions on options I've actually used.

formats.name: Levels
formats.idea_has: A progression from beginner to advanced

cards.name: Levels
cards.use_when: there's a progression from beginner to advanced, and most people are stuck low.
cards.needs: a concrete example for each level.

formats.name: Interview Clips
formats.idea_has: Footage of a conversation

cards.name: Interview Clips
cards.use_when: I have a recorded conversation with a hot take in it.
cards.needs: footage with a second person.

formats.name: Reaction
formats.idea_has: A clip worth responding to

cards.name: Explain it
cards.use_when: there's a clip people misread, and I know what's really going on.
cards.needs: a base clip I can stitch or duet.

cards.name: Comedy
cards.use_when: the clip looks bad at first, but it has a twist I can react to.
cards.needs: a base clip with a real twist.

formats.name: Skit / Humor
formats.idea_has: A funny or relatable situation I can act out

cards.name: Comedy
cards.use_when: a character gets something wrong in a way people know.
cards.needs: acting, often a second person.

cards.name: Heartfelt
cards.use_when: an acted scene is a way into an honest message I want to say to camera.
cards.needs: acting, plus a real message I mean.

formats.name: About Me
formats.idea_has: My background or origin story

cards.name: Origin story
cards.use_when: I'm introducing myself, telling how I got from where I started to where I am now.
cards.needs: my real story, with real moments, numbers and at least one low point.

cards.name: Everything I tried
cards.use_when: there were lots of attempts before one big win, and I can number them.
cards.needs: a real list of attempts, with real losses and numbers.

formats.name: Personal Update
formats.idea_has: News: a launch, a move, a milestone

cards.name: News as punchline
cards.use_when: something happened that changed things for me, and the setup makes the news hit harder.
cards.needs: real news.

cards.name: Big day plus lessons
cards.use_when: today is a big day, and it's making me think about a few truths.
cards.needs: a real big day.

cards.name: Launch
cards.use_when: we're launching something.
cards.needs: a real launch and a real credibility number.

formats.name: Day In The Life
formats.idea_has: A day that's different from what people picture

cards.name: Day In The Life
cards.use_when: my day is different from what people picture for someone like me.
cards.needs: footage of a real day.

formats.name: Episodic Series
formats.idea_has: A repeatable show idea

cards.name: Test series
cards.use_when: a repeatable show where each episode tests one thing and ends with a verdict or score.
cards.needs: a series idea I can keep going.

cards.name: Tutorial series
cards.use_when: a repeatable show where each episode teaches or makes one thing, with no verdict.
cards.needs: a series idea with enough episodes in it.

formats.name: Challenge
formats.idea_has: A goal I can chase on camera

cards.name: Challenge
cards.use_when: I'm chasing a goal on camera.
cards.needs: actually doing the challenge, with a clear number to hit.

close_calls: Problem Solution vs Tutorial: lead with the pain, it's Problem Solution. Lead with the thing they'll make, it's Tutorial.
Common Trap vs Problem Solution: the mistake is the interesting part, it's Common Trap. The fix is, it's Problem Solution.
Breakdowns vs Case Studies: a general "why" is a Breakdown. One real result, broken down, is a Case Study.

Breakdowns vs Scenarios: explaining how something works, or teaching a way of thinking or a mental model, is a Breakdown, even with a personal example. Scenarios only when the post is built on a "what if" or on a claim people will doubt plus a plan.
Breakdowns vs Tutorial: teaching a way of thinking is a Breakdown. Steps that end in something made or done is a Tutorial.
Listicle vs Ranking vs Levels: tips side by side is a Listicle. Judging options is a Ranking. Each one better than the last is Levels.
Hero's Journey vs Personal Learning: a climb from stuck to better is Hero's Journey. Something I didn't expect is Personal Learning.
Q&A vs Interview Clips: I'm answering on my own, it's Q&A. Someone else is in the footage, it's Interview Clips.
